Small repairs. Big projects. One local team. 29 Palms Handyman & Construction brings over 10 years of hands-on experience to residential, commercial, and military/government work. Small jobs are welcome, and larger projects are reviewed by scope. We serve Twentynine Palms, Joshua Tree, Yucca Valley, Hemet, Banning, Desert Hot Springs, Palm Springs, Big Bear, and nearby communities. We come to your property. Years of weather had taken their toll on the wood, leaving the surface faded and worn. Our team gave the entire deck the attention it needed, from prep work to the final finish, bringing it back to life with a clean, modern look that completely transformed the outdoor space. Now this deck is ready for backyard BBQs, family gatherings, and plenty more seasons to come. Whether you need a new deck, structural repairs, restoration, or professional staining, 4 Seasons Painting & Construction is here to help get the job done right. Serving Walla Walla and surrounding areas!

From the owner
Moldy roof sheathing we found above a bathroom ceiling in Moscow. We opened the ceiling during a bathroom remodel and found the roof sheathing above the shower soaked, black with mold in places, and starting to come apart. The shingles had been replaced a couple of years earlier, but the old sheathing under them was left in place without being checked. Water had been getting in before the new shingles went on, most likely through bad flashing where two roof planes meet. A camera scope showed a problem before demo, and opening the ceiling confirmed it. The next steps are containment, a Moldex mold treatment, drying out the framing, and replacing the damaged sheathing before any drywall goes back up. Mold left inside a ceiling keeps growing and releases spores into the air of the house, so it comes out before the room is closed in. If your roof was replaced and no one checked the sheathing underneath, ask your roofer whether they did. Moscow, ID

From the owner
If you are used to residential remodeling, a commercial project in Los Angeles changes who is involved, what is at stake, and how the work gets scheduled. Here is what is different from the client’s side. You are not the only decision maker. Property owners, landlords, tenants, and sometimes franchise or brand standards all have a say, so approvals can take more rounds than a homeowner would expect. Your business keeps running, or loses money while it doesn’t. That pushes commercial work toward phasing, night and weekend shifts, and planning around deliveries, staff, and customers. The rules are heavier. Accessibility, fire and life safety, occupancy, and signage can all come into play, along with stricter review of plans. Requirements depend on the property and how it will be used, so confirm them before you design. The systems are bigger. Electrical capacity, HVAC, plumbing, data, and lighting often need to support equipment and many people, not one household. Finishes also have a different job. They need to stand up to constant use and still match your brand. A contractor who has done this before plans around all of it from day one. Call us today to talk through your commercial project in Los Angeles.
